title: The value follows a change made in the staff window
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Have a valid Public API key for the test organization, the Public API documentation for staff, and a request tool (Postman or any tool that sends requests with that key).
  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Have a new staff member for this test, staff member A, on the built-in Parts Manager role, with Time Clock on and Technician on, enrolled at the test location only, leading no work.
  • Note staff member A's id as the Public API gives it (from GET /api/v1/staff).
  • Start on Settings, Staff.
custom_steps:
1. Send GET /api/v1/staff/<staff member A's id> with the API key.
  2. Open staff member A's Edit Staff Member window.
  3. Switch Technician off.
  4. Click Save & Close.
  5. Send GET /api/v1/staff/<staff member A's id> with the API key.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The record includes "technician": true.

Step 2:

  • The window shows Technician on.

Step 3:

  • Technician is off.

Step 4:

  • The window closes.

Step 5:

  • The record now includes "technician": false.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Technician Toggle", Confluence 977371146, version 17 (2 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 2 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11788, story SV-11879 (Story 1, Technician toggle on a staff member), story SV-11883 (Story 5, Public API - technician value on staff)

  • S5-R1: “Each staff record the Public API returns includes a read-only technician value: true when the person is active, their Technician toggle is on and their Time Clock is on (the same rule as the staff list column, S4-R1), otherwise false. A deactivated person is always false.”
  • S1-R6: “Switching Technician on or off changes nothing until the user saves the staff member with the window's existing Save. Once saved, the change applies to every technician list (Story 3) the next time each list loads (S1-E3).”
